text:
Vikram: Heads up — p99 on /generate (eu-west) spiked at ~08:43 but p50 stayed flat. wondering if this is a percentile calc bug or routing fallout?
TelemetryBot: Alert: endpoint=/generate region=eu-west metric=p99 increased 4.6x at 2024-05-03T08:43:12Z (alert id 8842). linked runbook: https://console/redwood/alerts/8842 :warning:
Anya: I pulled the raw samples quickly — overall sample_count for that endpoint dropped ~30% around 08:42. p50 unchanged because most short calls persisted; long-tail seems amplified.
Matt: can you paste the query you ran? curious if we're accidentally blending two different sample sets (eg. model_variant tag mismatch)
Anya: sure — here's the simplified query I ran against telemetry-store:```sql
SELECT bin, percentile_latency(50) as p50, percentile_latency(95) as p95, percentile_latency(99) as p99, count(*) as samples
FROM requests
WHERE endpoint = '/generate' AND region = 'eu-west' AND ts BETWEEN '2024-05-03T08:30:00Z' AND '2024-05-03T08:50:00Z'
GROUP BY bin;```
Anya: snippet of results (aggregated by 1m):```
08:40 - p50=210ms p95=620ms p99=1280ms samples=1200
08:42 - p50=215ms p95=650ms p99=6200ms samples=820
08:44 - p50=212ms p95=640ms p99=1350ms samples=1150
```
Kara: we rolled a routing canary around 08:41 — changed route policy for low-cost tier to prefer n1-small fallback for requests with "cost_hint: low". config snippet:```yaml
route_policy: cost_first
fallbacks:
  - pool: cheap-eu
    max_latency_ms: 2000
```
Kara: might explain why a small fraction got routed to a slower fallback which would blow up the tail.
Vikram: That fits — p50 flat but p99 spikes match a few requests that hit a very slow fallback instance. However the sample_count dip is concerning: why did samples drop while some requests got slower?
Matt: Two possibilities: (1) sampling logic excludes very long-running requests after a timeout (so sample_count drops but tail requests survive elsewhere), or (2) tag normalization bug split samples across groups. I've seen `model_version` vs `model:version` split before.
Anya: Checked tags — for a short window there were duplicate variant tags: some requests had `model_version=43a` others `model:version=43a`. That would create two groups and make each group's percentiles misleading.
Anya: quick grep from logs:```text
2024-05-03T08:41:09Z INFO request id=... tags={endpoint:/generate, model:version=43a, region:eu-west}
2024-05-03T08:41:10Z INFO request id=... tags={endpoint:/generate, model_version=43a, region:eu-west}
```
Matt: Yup. Aggregation service merges by tag name, so that split would reduce samples in the main group and concentrate the slow ones elsewhere — explains both drop in samples and p99 jump.
Kara: Good catch. The canary also changed routing metadata format (we updated `cost_hint` -> `cost_tier` as part of the rollout). that might have affected how the sampler evaluates which pool to sample.
eng-oncall: Should we rollback the routing canary? Current impact is high tail but low QPS impact.
Vikram: I'd prefer a targeted fix in telemetry/aggregation so the tag aliasing is handled, and then tighten the canary to not rewrite tag keys. Rollback only if we see sustained errors or customer complaints.
Anya: I can open a tiny PR to aggregation that treats `model_version` and `model:version` as aliases for 5m while we fix the caller. Also will add a dashboard column `samples` next to each percentile and show `min/max` latencies for context.
Matt: nice — can we also show the raw sample set size used to compute each percentile? UI idea: small tooltip "computed over N samples (filters applied)".
Kara: I'll patch the canary to stop rewriting tags and push a config change to `route_policy: cost_first` -> add `preserve_tags: true` for canaries. snippet:```yaml
canary_opts:
  preserve_tags: true
```
TelemetryBot: Deploy activity: canary/route-cost-first started by Kara (deploy id dc-9921) at 2024-05-03T08:41:00Z.
Anya: Opening PR now: #3126 (agg: alias model_version keys, dashboard: surface sample_count + min/max). I'll also add a short test to assert percentiles include sample count metadata.
Vikram: Great. Also can the console show a small warning when percentile computations use < 100 samples? helps avoid overreacting to tiny groups.
Matt: Agree. We should also add a nightly job to detect tag-key entropy spikes — when new tag keys appear for an endpoint it should create an alert.
eng-oncall: i'll stay on watch for 30m and escalate if it persists. ping me with the PR link.
Vikram: Thanks all — sounds like action items: Anya PR, Kara preserve_tags change, Matt follow-up on tag-entropy alert. If anything looks systemic we rollback. :thumbsup:
